name: write_file
description: Apply 1-16 file operations in array order. Example: {"operations":[{"path":"notes.txt","mode":"append","content":"text"}]}. Results correspond to operations by zero-based index. Relative paths use the session cwd. overwrite and append require content and create the file and parent directories. replace_text requires nonempty old_text and a new_text string; it changes exactly one literal occurrence, otherwise fails without writing. Empty new_text deletes that occurrence. replace_lines requires existing 1-based inclusive start_line and end_line, content, and lowercase expected_sha256. First read exactly those lines with read_file, then copy that result's sha256 into expected_sha256; it hashes the original selected bytes, including BOM and line endings. A changed selected span or missing line fails without writing. Empty content deletes the lines; a nonempty replacement without a final newline keeps the original separator before following lines. Invalid arguments reject the whole batch before any write. Runtime errors are reported per operation and later operations continue; completed writes are not rolled back. Abort skips remaining operations. Alternatively pass {"patch":"*** Begin Patch\n...\n*** End Patch"}, exclusively instead of operations. Supports Add File (+ lines), Update File (bare @@ context hunks), optional Move to, and Delete File. Unique exact context only; EOF and no-final-newline markers supported. Patch limits: 1 MiB, 64 paths, 16 MiB per file. Preflight all files before changes; symlinks and clobbering renames rejected. Runtime patch failure stops subsequent files and reports partial success. Successful writes publish bounded Files changed session history.

operations.description: Array of write operation objects; a runtime failure in one operation does not undo other successful operations.

path.description: File path, absolute or relative to the session cwd.

mode.description: overwrite/append use content; replace_text uses old_text/new_text; replace_lines uses a guarded line range and content.

content.description: Whole content for overwrite, suffix for append, or replacement lines for replace_lines. Empty content is allowed.

old_text.description: Nonempty literal text for replace_text; must occur exactly once.

new_text.description: Replacement for replace_text; empty text deletes the match.

end_line.description: Inclusive last existing line for replace_lines; must not precede start_line.

expected_sha256.description: Lowercase sha256 from read_file for exactly the selected original lines; guards against changed bytes.

patch.description: Documented raw text patch dialect; mutually exclusive with operations.
